name: Indian (Vedic)
description: The 27/28 nakshatras (lunar mansions) of Vedic astronomy with their junction stars (yogataras), plus the Saptarshi sages and the Pole Star Dhruva.
source: Stellarium sky cultures (github.com/Stellarium/stellarium-skycultures) - indian/index.json and description.md (authors: Tanmoy Saha, Vishvas Vasuki and the sanskrit-coders community; reworked by Susanne M. Hoffmann)
Nakshatra: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakshatra (cited by Stellarium for the mansions)
Stars not in constellations.json taken from HYG v4.1 (github.com/astronexus/HYG-Database)
license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Stellarium indian sky culture: "CC BY-SA"; share-alike applies). HYG v4.1 data: CC BY-SA 4.0. Omission: the twelve Rashi (sidereal zodiac signs) are 30-degree sectors with no star figures in any source, so none are included.

figures.name: Aśvinī
figures.story: Nakshatra 1 of the 28-fold list (27 in the later system, with Abhijit omitted); a division of the Moon's path used for ritual timing and the calendar. Star identification follows the Stellarium Vedic sky culture; a one-star line marks the yogatara (junction star).

figures.name: Saptarṣi
figures.story: The seven stars of the Big Dipper, each assigned to a Vedic sage (names as in the Stellarium Vedic sky culture): Kratu (Dubhe), Pulaha (Merak), Pulastya (Phecda), Atri (Megrez), Aṅgiras (Alioth), Vasiṣṭha (Mizar) and Marīci (Alkaid).

figures.name: Arundhatī
figures.story: Alcor (HIP 65477), the faint companion of Mizar (Vasiṣṭha), is named Arundhatī after the sage's wife in the Stellarium Vedic sky culture.

figures.name: Dhruva
figures.story: Dhruva is the Pole Star (Polaris, HIP 11767). The line runs along the two pointer stars of the Saptarṣi bowl (Kratu, Pulaha) to Dhruva.
